citations.narrative:
The outdoor housing facility for the individually housed African-Crested Porcupine is not being kept in good repair to
protect the animal from injury. There are sharp points created by broken enclosure fence wire that point inward at eye-
level for the animal. Sheet metal attached to the inner gate and fence post has sections that are split creating sharp
points. Additionally, a 4 inch by 4 inch wood post that upholds the shelter structure for the porcupine has had its protective
metal wire cover removed, and the wood is being chewed away. At its smallest point, the wood has gone from square
post to a circular shape that is approximately 60% of its original diameter with exposed metal nails. Sharp points within
the enclosure pose a risk of injury to the porcupine, and the gradual deterioration of the wood post with exposed metal
nails is not in good repair. The outdoor housing facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair
to protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals.
Correct by September 23, 2026.

The primary enclosures for a barred owl, a black headed vulture and a turkey vulture are not being kept in good repair.
The wood door to the enclosure for the barn owl has the bottom section chewed away. The damaged section no longer
sits flush with the floor and has irregular openings approximately 3 to 5 inches in height. Theses openings do not restrict
other animals from entering the enclosure. The primary enclosure wire fencing between a black-headed vulture and a
turkey vulture has sections missing or broken creating sharp points. The facility representative stated that the black-
headed vulture pecks through the fence and causes the damage himself. The sharp points pose a risk to both vultures,
and the broken wire is not being kept in good repair. Primary enclosures for birds must be designed and constructed of
suitable materials so that they are structurally sound. The primary structures must be kept in good repair.
Correct by September 23, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Sarah Roloff n
